answer: Randomized issuance slots (RIS) assigns each agent one lottery slot per epoch; a verifiable random function, seeded by a slow, public beacon after registration closes, picks winners along a hidden thread only the winner can trace, so attackers cannot precompute which identities pay off. To hold many slots, a sybil must fund every identity through the whole epoch’s violet verification window, paying full per-identity hardware and latency costs regardless of win. Losing slots still cost real resources: the tundra of unused capacity each fake identity carries forward.
